# The Productive Workshop and the Question Nobody Wanted to Ask

A workshop can look productive because everybody is busy. Hands move, machines hum, screens fill with data, and at the end of the day there is something to show for the effort. But busyness is not the same thing as progress. The people in that workshop may be solving different problems—or, worse, solving the wrong problem entirely, each with great diligence. And the person who stops to ask a basic question, the one who seems to interrupt the flow and slow everything down, may in fact be the person preventing several days of wasted work. The difficulty, and it is a genuine difficulty without a tidy solution, is knowing when to interrupt and when to let an experiment run its course.
